title: Independent evaluation finds Google Flood Hub and GloFAS forecasts skillful beyond four days in Mali's frequently flooded regions, suggesting seven-day Red Cross early-action triggers
summary: Independent study finds Google Flood Hub skillful beyond 4-day lead time, enough for 7-day Mali Red Cross early action triggers.
account: A peer-reviewed study in the Journal of Flood Risk Management (published online 16 September 2026; volume 19, issue 3, September 2026) by researchers from the Netherlands Red Cross 510 data team, Utrecht University, the EU Joint Research Centre, Politecnico di Milano and the University of Twente evaluated Google Flood Hub (GFH), Google's AI-based flood forecasting service, against GloFAS and the Mali Red Cross's existing Early Action Protocol trigger, using discharge observations and district-level impact data. The existing trigger relies on upstream water levels and is limited to a four-day lead time. The authors report that GloFAS and GFH demonstrate sufficient skill for early action beyond a four-day lead time in frequently flooded regions, suggesting early action plans could operate with a seven-day lead time and span a larger area. No realized early action is documented.
purpose: AI-based riverine flood forecasting for ungauged basins to support early warning and anticipatory action.
deployer: Evaluated for the Mali Red Cross Early Action Protocol; not documented as an operational trigger
taxonomy_note: A forecast-skill evaluation is read as task accuracy; no early action is documented.
